name: TAG-28
keyCapabilities: Command and Control of Multi-protocol Communication
Persistence via Registry Keys & Web Shells
Large Language Model (LLM) Integration for Tool Development
recommendedActions: Patch critical infrastructure and Perimeter devices for CVE-2024-39717.
Mitigate risk from CVE-2022-38028 by updating internal systems.
Harden Microsoft Exchange and Outlook servers against unauthorized access (GONEPOSTAL) and script execution.
Implement MFA across all enterprise accounts, specifically targeting high-privilege and administrator roles.
Monitor network logs for usage of certutil, vssadmin, and wevtutil to identify credential dumping or log manipulation.
Segment SOHO devices and prioritize securing IoT/Network hardware with unique credentials.
Block known command-and-control schemes over public platforms like Google Drive or through atypical ports (7777).
Implement stricter outbound controls on standard network tools like PowerShell if not required for business operations.
Deploy endpoint detection capabilities to flag hidden data in steganographic formats or non-standard encrypted packets.
Audit and secure critical documentation by preventing unauthorized DDE or macro executions from external emails.
campaignsText: TAG-28/APT28 demonstrates a stable and consistent operational tempo, with active campaigns lasting several years. They are known for long-running operations such as the 'Nearest Neighbor Campaign' (2022–2024), where they targeted entities involved in Ukraine intelligence through a mix of Wi-Fi proximity exploitation and credential theft. Their historical activity includes high-profile interventions like the 2016 U.S. election interference and multi-year campaigns targeting European energy infrastructure in coordination with (or utilizing tactics shared by) the Sandworm Team. The actor has also been observed in more recent, localized operations against Indian media conglomerates and critical government infrastructure platforms, as well as global cyber-espionage using sophisticated tools to target foreign defense contractors.
description: TAG-28 (predominantly identified as APT28/Fancy Bear) is a sophisticated Russian state-sponsored threat actor engaged in high-level cyber espionage, information theft, and infrastructure disruption. The group leverages complex evasion techniques, multiple malware families like Winnti, and advanced technologies including LLM-integrated tools to target government, energy, and critical infrastructure globally.
goals: TAG-28 primarily executes operations for strategic intelligence gathering and political espionage. Their targets include high-value government agencies, defense contractors, energy providers, and critical infrastructure across Western and Asian nations. They focus specifically on actors involved in the Ukraine conflict, as well as sectors like telemedia and banking to cultivate long-term influence and gather sensitive data.
